sections.html:
Property records are not available online right now. The Clay County Clerk has digitized deed records back to the 1960s, but you need to call or visit the clerk's office in Henrietta. Ask for the record by owner name, legal description or instrument number.

Two limits apply. The clerk gives no legal advice and has no duty to search the records for you (Attorney General opinion WW-607). Hire a title company or attorney for that.

Find the clerk in the Courthouse Annex, 214 N. Main Street, Henrietta, TX 76365. Mail goes to P.O. Box 548. Call (940) 538-4631 or fax (940) 264-4160. The doors open 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, minus a daily lunch closure from noon to 1:00 p.m.

  • The office closes for major holidays.
  • It may close for court hearings, training or bad weather, so call before a long drive.
  • Historic Commissioners' Court record books from the 1870s have been restored and are kept in the clerk's office.

sections.h2: Photo ID to file a deed
sections.html:
Bring a government photo ID. Senate Bill 16, effective September 1, 2025, added Local Government Code 191.010(b). The clerk must require photo ID from whoever presents a document for the real property records, must copy it, and must reject the filing if the person refuses.

The law is a statewide deed fraud measure. It also tightens criminal penalties for real property theft and fraud, lets victims seek restitution and a no-fee judicial voiding of a fraudulent deed, and sets stronger standards for notaries. If you plan to mail a deed, ask the clerk how the ID rule applies to documents delivered by a title company.

The first page costs $25 in total, and each added page costs $4, under the fee schedule effective September 1, 2025. Other recording fees are below.

The $25 first-page figure is a $10 archive fee, a $5 recording fee and a $10 records management fee. Each name to be indexed beyond five adds $0.25.

sections.h2: Mistakes that add fees or get a deed refused
sections.html:
Format errors raise the price or stop the filing:

  • No grantee mailing address on a deed signed after December 31, 1981 brings a penalty equal to the greater of twice the filing fee or $25, on top of regular fees.
  • No clear heading at the top of the first page doubles the filing fee for that page.
  • Names not legibly typed or printed under each signature double the fee for that page.
  • Printed type must be no smaller than 8 point (Local Government Code 191.007).
  • The deed needs original signatures and a notarized acknowledgment (Property Code 12.001(b)).

Copies run $1.00 a page and certification adds $5.00 per document. A notice of trustee sale is $2.00, and a bounced check costs you $30.

Deeds are recorded where the land sits, and in Clay County that means the clerk in Henrietta. Warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, deed of trust releases and powers of attorney all go through the same counter. Commissioners courts may waive recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs, so ask the clerk whether Clay County does.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell a Clay County house
sections.html:
Before you hand a deed to a buyer, make sure you can answer three questions. Whose names are on the current deed, and are all of them alive and able to sign? Is every mortgage released of record? Is the homestead exemption on file with the appraisal district?

Because records are not online, plan on a phone call or a trip. Ask your title company to pull the chain of title. Plan for the photo ID rule when the deed is filed, keep your own ID current and with you, bring the grantee's full mailing address so the deed is not penalized, and call the clerk before driving to Henrietta. After filing, keep the file-stamped copy, because the buyer's lender and your own tax records will both want it.

When an owner has died, the house may not be sellable until probate is filed. A base probate or guardianship filing is $360, and $418 when a citation is issued and posted by the sheriff. A will left for safekeeping with the clerk costs $16. The clerk also has a guardianship registration form and civil court cost instructions.

The clerk cannot recommend a route, so a Texas attorney is the person to ask which one fits the estate. Having the death certificate, the will if there is one, and a list of heirs ready speeds the first conversation.

The district values property and processes exemptions. It never levies, sets or collects taxes, so call the proper tax office for amounts owed. Its site, claycad.org, carries forms, an interactive map, protest hearing information and an oil and gas FAQ.

  • Homestead exemption: you owned and lived in the house on January 1 as your principal residence. Up to 20 acres of residential land can be covered.
  • Filing window: January 1 through April 30 of the tax year. A late homestead claim is accepted up to two years after the taxes turn delinquent.
  • Over 65: the claim can be filed up to one year after the 65th birthday, with proof of age.
  • Mobile homes can be set up as improvement-only accounts if you file a request for separate taxation with the title or a verified purchase contract.

Protests are normally due May 15, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if later. A plain letter works, and no official form is required.

sections.h2: Clay County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Clay County is thinly settled: 10,764 people in the July 2025 estimate, up from 10,218 at the 2020 census, across 1,088.76 square miles. It has 5,247 housing units, and owners occupy 84.0% of 4,289 households. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $171,500 (2020 to 2024), and gross rent has a median of $811. New construction is rare, with just 8 building permits in 2025.

With so few sales, a comparable house may be miles away. Ask a title company for recent recorded deed prices in your part of the county.

faqs.q: Are Clay County property records available online?
faqs.a: No. Deed records are digitized back to the 1960s, but property records are not online. Call (940) 538-4631 or visit the annex in Henrietta.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Clay County Clerk?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The annex shuts for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m., and bad weather, training or hearings can close it, so call first.

faqs.q: Do I need a photo ID to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Local Government Code 191.010(b), added by Senate Bill 16 effective September 1, 2025, the clerk must require photo ID from the person presenting a real property document, copy it and reject the filing if the person refuses.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: Page one is $25 and each added page is $4. A missing grantee address, a missing heading or unreadable printed names bring extra penalties.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Clay County?
faqs.a: Not the appraisal district. Call the proper tax office for amounts. The appraisal district's site has a separate Pay Taxes Online link for that purpose.
